suggested_draft:

Our article "Diagnosing elevated response latency" describes this situation. Compare median and 95th percentile latency on the metrics page. A large gap points to contention or queueing rather than a uniformly slower service. [DOC-PERF-001] Check memory utilisation across instances. Sustained utilisation above eighty per cent typically shows up as latency before it shows up as failure. [DOC-PERF-001] Review the dependency timing breakdown on the trace view to identify whether the time is being spent in your service or waiting on another. [DOC-PERF-001] Adjust the autoscaling policy if load is predictable. Scaling on request count responds sooner than scaling on processor utilisation. [DOC-PERF-001]

suggested_draft:
Hello,

Our article "Pagination and handling large result sets" describes this situation. Use cursor pagination for anything that may change while you iterate. Offset pagination will skip or repeat records when items are inserted mid-iteration. [DOC-API-002] Pass the next_cursor value from each response as the cursor parameter of the following request, and stop when it is null. [DOC-API-002] Keep page size at or below two hundred. Larger requests are rejected rather than truncated. [DOC-API-002] For very large extracts, use the export endpoint, which runs asynchronously and returns a download link. [DOC-API-002]

relevant_articles.title: Database connection pool exhaustion
Autoscaling behaviour and instance limits
Diagnosing elevated response latency

suggested_draft:
Hello,

Our article "Database connection pool exhaustion" describes this situation. Calculate the total possible connections as pool size multiplied by maximum instances, and compare it against your plan's connection limit. [DOC-PERF-003] Reduce the per-instance pool size rather than raising the limit. A large number of small pools is usually the wrong shape for a scaled service. [DOC-PERF-003] Look for queries that hold a transaction open across a network call to another service, which is the most common cause of leaks of this kind. [DOC-PERF-003] Consider a connection proxy if the instance count must remain high, so that pooling happens once rather than per instance. [DOC-PERF-003]
